value.method: contention sense: read set = committed units with prefix booking/<box>/ (the subject's box); a committed booking contends iff ALL of: status is "active" only (done, cancelled, preempted and expired bookings are inert); its id differs from the candidate's id (a booking never contends with itself -- a committed row whose id equals the candidate's id is excluded even when its producer differs); its producer differs from the candidate's producer (a same-producer overlap is a renewal, not contention); its checkby is null or >= the candidate start (a booking whose check-by passed before the candidate starts is dead by the board protocol); seat rules -- equal seats contend iff the seat is in {zcode, mcode, claude-code, gpu, stage, kimi, box}, "box" contends with every seat, other distinct seats do not contend; and strict interval overlap candidate.start < other.end and other.start < candidate.end (touching endpoints do not contend). Value reports every contender sorted by id, their count, the maximum contender rank (-1 when none), the highest-rank contender's id (ties: smallest id, null when none), and "unclassified": the sorted seat strings -- the candidate's seat and the seats of status-"active" rows under the prefix -- that are in neither the exclusive set nor {"detached"}. Rank otherwise plays no part in contention itself.

authority sense: read set = log entries passing three filters -- entry kind is "execution", the entry body's producer is "operator", and the entry's applied writes include a write to unit authority/<producer>. Among those writes the LATEST wins: its value (an integer) is the ceiling, so a later lower grant is a downward revocation; grants is the count of such writes. Only operator-authored writes count: a producer's own write to authority/<self> may land in units under policy/1 but fails the producer filter, so it is visible in the log and inert here. The unit's current value alone is not evidence of a grant. No operator grant -> ceiling null, grants 0.
